name: Avus moto
notes: The short configuration of Berlin's AVUS, turning back at a tight hairpin well before the far end of the Grunewald and cutting the lap to 8.327 km — a little over 4 km of straight in each direction instead of nine. That hairpin had always been there and had been the motorcycle course since the 1920s; the cars inherited it in 1938, when the old Südkurve was torn out to make an interchange for the growing Reichsautobahn. The banked Nordkurve of 1937 still closes the northern end, so the character is unchanged: almost the whole lap flat out, with everything decided by how late you dare stay on the throttle into the turns. Driven counter-clockwise.
author: Legion
